display.purpose: Hero headline only, capped at 17ch. Set in the Neo-Grotesque body face at 700 with -0.038em tracking; there is no separate display family.

lede.purpose: The paragraph directly beneath a display or headline, ink-2, capped at 46rem.

body.purpose: All prose. Capped at 34-40rem so lines land at 65-75 characters inside the 72rem wrap.

label.purpose: Monospace Code, reserved for data, identifiers, measurements, hosts, SHAs, grades and column heads. Never prose.

figure.purpose: Industrial stack on numerals and short figures only, as a progressive enhancement that degrades to the sans.

shadows.name: resting-lift
shadows.purpose: Objects that sit slightly above the page at rest: the primary button, the week figure, the promotion rail. Dark mode: 0 1px 2px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 0 4px 14px -6px rgba(0,0,0,0.6).

shadows.name: responding-lift
shadows.purpose: Hover only: the primary button and the route cards. Dark mode: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 0 26px 52px -24px rgba(0,0,0,0.8).

shadows.name: inset-hairline
shadows.purpose: The drawn edge on recessed calendar cells; a border, not a lift.

motion.name: ease-response
motion.purpose: The 140-160ms hover transform on buttons and route cards.

motion.name: ease-wake
motion.purpose: Exponential ease-out for the one authored moment: the week calendar's used hours arriving over 560ms.

motion.name: wake-stagger
motion.purpose: Per-cell delay from an inline index, with animation-fill-mode: backwards from an already-visible default. The whole block is gated behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action a page most wants taken; accent-filled, resting lift, rises on hover.
components.html: Start building on the model
components.css: .ds-btn { display: inline-block; font: 600 0.975rem/1.65 var(--font-sans, Inter, Roboto, Arial, sans-serif); letter-spacing: -0.006em; text-decoration: none; white-space: nowrap; padding: 0.72rem 1.35rem; border-radius: 7px; border: 1px solid transparent; transition: transform 140ms cubic-bezier(.2,.7,.3,1), box-shadow 140ms, background-color 140ms, border-color 140ms; } .ds-btn-primary { background: var(--accent, #067a68); color: var(--on-accent, #fff); box-shadow: var(--shadow-1, 0 1px 2px rgba(12,16,21,0.05), 0 4px 12px -5px rgba(12,16,21,0.12)); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { background: var(--accent-deep, #04564a); transform: translateY(-1px); box-shadow: var(--shadow-2, 0 2px 4px rgba(12,16,21,0.05), 0 22px 44px -22px rgba(12,16,21,0.25)); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #067a68); outline-offset: 3px; border-radius: 3px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn, .ds-btn:hover { transform: none; transition: none; } }

components.name: Ledger Entry
components.description: The site's structural unit: a claim, its body capped at 36rem, and a mono receipt line naming the mechanism that produces it. Divided by a soft hairline, not boxed.
components.html:
Failure that stays small

One person's process serves one person's data. A panic in someone's request path takes down their process; the next request starts it again.

mechanism: blast radius of one · multi-upstream routes · five-minute snapshots

components.css: .ds-week { margin: 0; padding: 1.4rem 1.5rem 1.5rem; border: 1px solid var(--rule, rgba(12,16,21,0.11)); border-radius: 11px; background: var(--surface, #fff); box-shadow: var(--shadow-1, 0 1px 2px rgba(12,16,21,0.05), 0 4px 12px -5px rgba(12,16,21,0.12)); font-family: var(--font-sans, Inter, Roboto, Arial, sans-serif); } .ds-week h2 { margin: 0 0 1rem; font: 680 1.15rem/1.12 inherit; letter-spacing: -0.015em; color: var(--ink, #0c1015); } .ds-cal { display: grid; gap: 3px; grid-template-columns: auto repeat(8, minmax(0, 1fr)); align-items: center; } .ds-day { font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.62rem; letter-spacing: 0.08em; color: var(--muted, #667385); padding-right: 0.5rem; } .ds-cal i { aspect-ratio: 1; border-radius: 1.5px; background: var(--bg-sunk, #f2f3f7); box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px var(--rule-soft, rgba(12,16,21,0.06)); } .ds-cal i.on { background: var(--accent, #067a68); box-shadow: none; } .ds-week .ds-data { display: block; margin-top: 0.85rem; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.775rem; letter-spacing: 0.06em; color: var(--muted, #667385); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) { .ds-cal i.on { animation: ds-wake 560ms cubic-bezier(.16,1,.3,1) backwards; animation-delay: calc(var(--i) * 48ms + 320ms); } } @keyframes ds-wake { from { background: var(--bg-sunk, #f2f3f7); transform: scale(0.5); } 55% { background: var(--accent, #067a68); transform: scale(1.35); } to { background: var(--accent, #067a68); transform: scale(1); } }

components.css: .ds-rail { display: flex; flex-wrap: wrap; align-items: stretch; gap: 0.6rem; padding: 1.4rem; border: 1px solid var(--rule, rgba(12,16,21,0.11)); border-radius: 10px; background: var(--surface, #fff); box-shadow: var(--shadow-1, 0 1px 2px rgba(12,16,21,0.05), 0 4px 12px -5px rgba(12,16,21,0.12)); } .ds-stop { flex: 1 1 9rem; display: grid; gap: 0.4rem; justify-items: center; padding: 0.9rem 0.6rem; border-radius: 7px; background: var(--bg-sunk, #f2f3f7); } .ds-stop-final { background: var(--accent-soft, rgba(6,122,104,0.10)); outline: 1px solid var(--accent, #067a68); } .ds-stop b { font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.85rem; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; color: var(--ink, #0c1015); } .ds-sha { font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.85rem; color: var(--accent, #067a68); font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums; } .ds-to { align-self: center; color: var(--muted, #667385); font-size: 1.1rem; } .ds-foot { flex-basis: 100%; padding-top: 0.4rem; text-align: center; font-family: var(--font-mono, ui-monospace, Menlo, monospace); font-size: 0.78rem; letter-spacing: 0.05em; color: var(--muted, #667385); } @media (max-width: 34rem) { .ds-to { display: none; } }

narrative.overview:
This is an instrument face, not a brochure. Every claim on these pages arrives attached to the machinery that produces it, and the visual system is built to make that pairing legible: a heading, a hairline, and a mono receipt line underneath. Nothing glows to seem important. The pages read exciting, modern and assertive — deliberately not the warm paper-and-serif world rastrillo.org already owns.

The whole world ships under the constraints of the architecture it describes: one hand-written stylesheet, no build step, no JavaScript, no fetched fonts. That constraint is the source of the system's most distinctive decision — the six CARLOS letter marks and the wordmark are drawn as inline SVG paths on a shared construction grid, because no installed stack carries a condensed industrial capital everywhere. Editing a mark means editing path geometry, not a font-family.

Structure is carried by rules, not by boxes. Sections are separated by a one-pixel hairline and a generous bay of vertical space; list items inside a section are separated by an even softer hairline. Cards exist, but only four things in the entire build are cards, and each earned it. Light and dark are both first-class: every token has a value in each, and the near-black ground (#0a0c10) is as much the house as the paper white.
keyCharacteristics: Drawn letterforms on a 100x140 grid; no display face anywhere
One accent per page, teal on /, blue on /platform/ — siblings, never identical
Hairline rules as the primary divider; cards as an exception that must be argued for
A four-step signal ramp that only ever encodes app trust class
Exactly one authored motion moment on the whole site
Mono reserved for data, identifiers and measurement — never for prose

rules.name: The Sibling Accent Rule
rules.body: A page declares exactly one accent, as four tokens (--accent, --accent-deep, --accent-soft, --on-accent) in a small inline :root block covering both colour schemes. Sibling pages must be visibly related and never identical. A page never mixes two accents.

rules.name: The Signal Reservation Rule
rules.body: --sig-s/a/b/c encode app trust class only. They may not be borrowed for emphasis, charts, status pills, or decoration. If a surface needs amber or coral for any other reason, it does not get them.

rules.name: The Two Hairlines Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two divider weights. --rule separates sections and outlines cards; --rule-soft separates items within a section. A third weight is a sign the hierarchy is wrong.

rules.name: The Drawn Letter Rule
rules.body: The six CARLOS letters and the wordmark are inline SVG paths on a shared 100x140 construction grid, cropped by viewBox="11 11 78 118" (wordmark 11 11 518 118, letters advanced 88 units apart). One stroke weight per context — 21 for the section plates, 18 for the wordmark — with stroke-linecap: butt (square on the wordmark), stroke-linejoin: miter, stroke: currentColor and fill: none, so a mark inherits its colour from the accent. Changing a mark means editing path geometry. Never substitute a font-family for a mark, and never introduce a fetched display face to imitate one.

rules.name: The Mono Is Data Rule
rules.body: --font-mono is for measurements, identifiers, hostnames, SHAs, grades, units and column heads. It is never used for prose and never worn as a "technical" costume. Its companion: any number that is a measurement sets in font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums.

rules.name: The Progressive Figure Rule
rules.body: --font-stencil (Industrial) is an enhancement, not a dependency: it appears only on numerals and short figures, and its last fallback is var(--font-sans). A surface must read correctly when that stack resolves to nothing special.

rules.name: The Zero Fetch Rule
rules.body: The site binds to no fetched font and no JavaScript. Every face is a Modern Font Stacks system stack. A design that needs a webfont is a design this site does not ship.

rules.name: The Rule-Not-Box Rule
rules.body: Sections and list items are divided by a hairline and space. Reach for a border-boxed container only when the content is genuinely a discrete object; four exist on the whole site.

rules.name: The Own Breakpoint Rule
rules.body: Each pattern declares the width at which its own content stops working (26rem, 34rem, 46rem, 48rem, 52rem, 60rem, 64rem). There is no device-named breakpoint scale, and new patterns should not invent one.

rules.name: The Flat-Until-It-Responds Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are flat at rest unless they are one of the four cards. Shadow escalates only from --shadow-1 to --shadow-2, and only on hover. There is no third shadow and no shadow on text, icons or rules.

dos: Do divide with hairlines and space first; a card must be a discrete object you can name, not a way to group paragraphs.
Do declare a page's accent as the four accent tokens in a small inline :root block covering both colour schemes, and give every new token a light and a dark value.
Do attach every claim to its mechanism — the ledger's mono receipt line is the system's way of saying "check this".
Do set measurements, identifiers, grades, hosts, SHAs and column heads in mono with tabular numerals.
Do draw new letterforms as inline SVG on the 100x140 grid at the existing stroke weight, caps and joins, with stroke: currentColor and fill: none.
Do cap prose at 34-40rem inside the 72rem wrap so lines land at 65-75 characters.
Do let each pattern choose the width at which its own content breaks.
Do theme the surfaces you did not draw: selection, scrollbar, focus ring, underline offset.
Do gate any animation behind prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference and make the un-animated state the complete one.
donts: Don't use the signal ramp (--sig-s/a/b/c) for anything but app trust class.
Don't fetch a font or add JavaScript; the site ships under the same rules as the architecture it describes.
Don't set a letter mark or the wordmark in a typeface, and don't add a display face — the drawn marks are the display voice.
Don't put prose in mono, or use mono to make a passage look technical.
Don't add a third shadow, a third hairline weight, or a shadow on text, icons or rules.
Don't mix two accents on one page, or use the sibling page's accent as a secondary colour.
Don't add a second animated moment; the waking week is the site's one piece of motion.
Don't introduce a device-named breakpoint scale or a global grid; the patterns carry their own.
